### BoK Gate check (v3 — MCORCH Master Execution Protocol)

For each BoK suite in `docs/bok/<slug>/`, verify completeness:
```bash
for slug in $(ls docs/bok/ 2>/dev/null); do
  if [ "$slug" = "security" ]; then
    required_sec=(00-deepsearch-blueprint 01-brd-security 02-srs-secure-spec 03-sdd-hardening-architecture 04-fmea-security)
    missing=()
    for doc in "${required_sec[@]}"; do
      [ -f "docs/bok/security/$doc.md" ] || missing+=("$doc")
    done
    [ ${#missing[@]} -eq 0 ] && echo "✅ security — BoK complete (ciso-4-artifact)" || echo "⚠️ security — missing: ${missing[*]}"
    continue
  fi
  required=(00-index 01-mrd 02-brd 03-prd 04-frd 05-sdd 06-data-model 07-process-flow 08-quality-metrics)
  missing=()
  for doc in "${required[@]}"; do
    [ -f "docs/bok/$slug/$doc.md" ] || missing+=("$doc")
  done
  [ ${#missing[@]} -eq 0 ] && echo "✅ $slug — BoK complete" || echo "⚠️ $slug — missing: ${missing[*]}"
done
```

If the user mentions working on a **new module / complex feature / integration / architectural change**:
- Check whether `docs/bok/<expected-slug>/` exists with all 9 docs.
- If missing: surface in the **ALERTAS** section as a critical block per CLAUDE.md MCORCH Master Execution Protocol.
- Recommend `/bok-scribe <idea summary>` before any code is written.

## Rules

- **TypeScript errors → report immediately.** If there are TS errors, list them under ALERTAS. Do not start implementing new features until errors are resolved (unless the user explicitly asks to proceed despite errors).
- **Unhealthy containers → report with triage.** Suggest the fix command if known (e.g., `docker compose restart mcorch-vector-engine` for chroma).
- **Uncommitted changes → describe, do not commit.** Only describe what exists in the working tree; committing is the user's call.
- **Keep the brief tight.** No padding. No repetition of CLAUDE.md architecture. The user already knows the architecture — they need the delta: what changed, what's broken, what's next.
- **Pending Actions priority order:** CRITICAL (before first client) > NON-CRITICAL > Phase Zeta > Core v3 > Epsilon v9.
- **Knowledge Mesh numbers:** use `GraphRAG State` section from HANDOFF.md as the source. Do not invent counts.

The code network query is slow (OTD-UCANVAS-PERF ~30s), so waits are generous.\n// Run: bun run scripts/qa/audit-universe-ui.ts   (use --no-vision only as an explicit, logged exception)\nimport { chromium } from 'playwright';\nimport { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js';\nimport { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'fs';\nimport { spawnSync } from 'child_process';\nimport { join } from 'path';\n\nconst ROOT = '/home/gcrUX/htdocs/constellation-orchestra';\nconst envPath = join(ROOT, '.env');\nif (existsSync(envPath)) {\n  const raw = readFileSync(envPath, 'utf-8');\n  for (const line of raw.split('\\n')) {\n    const m = line.match(/^([^#=\\s][^=]*)=(.*)$/);\n    if (m) process.env[m[1].trim()] = m[2].trim().replace(/^[\"']|[\"']$/g, '');\n  }\n}\n\nconst supabaseUrl = process.env.SUPABASE_URL;\nconst serviceKey = process.env.SB_SECRET_KEY ?? process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY;\nif (!supabaseUrl || !serviceKey) {\n  console.error('\u274c Missing Supabase credentials in env.');\n  process.exit(1);\n}\n\nconst redirectTarget = 'https://login.mcorch.com/dashboard/universe';\n\nasync function runAudit() {\n  console.log('\ud83d\ude80 Starting Unified Sensorial Canvas (Universo) E2E audit...');\n  const supabase = createClient(supabaseUrl!, serviceKey!, { auth: { autoRefreshToken: false, persistSession: false } });\n\n  console.log('\ud83d\udd10 Generating one-time Magic Link for gabrielcall@gmail.com...');\n  const { data: linkData, error: linkErr } = await supabase.auth.admin.generateLink({\n    type: 'magiclink',\n    email: 'gabrielcall@gmail.com',\n    options: { redirectTo: redirectTarget },\n  });\n  if (linkErr || !linkData?.properties?.action_link) {\n    console.error('\u274c Failed to generate magic login link:', linkErr);\n    process.exit(1);\n  }\n  const magicLink = linkData.properties.action_link;\n  console.log('\ud83d\udd17 Magic Link generated.');\n\n  console.log('\ud83c\udf10 Launching headless Chromium...');\n  const browser = await chromium.launch({ headless: true });\n  const context = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: 1920, height: 1080 } });\n  const page = await context.newPage();\n\n  console.log('\u2708\ufe0f Navigating via magic link...');\n  await page.goto(magicLink);\n  try {\n    await page.waitForURL('**/dashboard/universe*', { timeout: 20000 });\n    console.log(`\ud83d\udccd Redirected to: ${page.url().split('#')[0]}`);\n  } catch {\n    console.error('\u274c Timeout waiting for auth redirection. Current URL:', page.url());\n    await browser.close();\n    process.exit(1);\n  }\n\n  // Structural assert: the Unified Sensorial Canvas HUD must mount.\n  console.log('\u23f3 Waiting for the Unified Sensorial Canvas HUD...');\n  try {\n    await page.waitForFunction(\n      () => document.body.innerText.includes('Unified Sensorial Canvas'),\n      { timeout: 20000 },\n    );\n  } catch {\n    console.error('\u274c Assert Failed: \"Unified Sensorial Canvas\" HUD not found.');\n    await browser.close();\n    process.exit(1);\n  }\n\n  // Force the 'universe' view so the screenshot shows the full fusion (code + memory + synapses).\n  try {\n    await page.getByTitle('Vis\u00e3o: Universo').click({ timeout: 5000 });\n    console.log('\ud83e\ude90 Switched to Universo view.');\n  } catch {\n    console.warn('\u26a0\ufe0f Could not click the Universo toggle (continuing with default view).');\n  }\n\n  // The code network query is slow (OTD-UCANVAS-PERF). Wait for the \"N\u00f3s\" stat to become numeric\n  // (loading shows \"\u2026\"), up to 75s, then let R3F settle.\n  console.log('\u23f3 Waiting for network data to settle (code query is slow)...');\n  try {\n    await page.waitForFunction(\n      () => {\n        const t = document.body.innerText;\n        // The N\u00f3s stat renders \"\u2026\" while loading; a digit means the graph resolved.\n        const m = t.match(/N[\u00f3o]s\\s*\\n?\\s*([\\d.\u00a0]+)/i);\n        return !!m && /\\d/.test(m[1]);\n      },\n      { timeout: 75000 },\n    );\n    console.log('\ud83d\udcca Code network resolved.');\n  } catch {\n    console.warn('\u26a0\ufe0f Timeout waiting for the code network stat; capturing anyway.');\n  }\n\n  const canvasCount = await page.locator('canvas').count();\n  console.log(`\ud83c\udfa8 WebGL <canvas> elements: ${canvasCount}`);\n  if (canvasCount === 0) {\n    console.error('\u274c Assert Failed: no <canvas> (R3F) element rendered.');\n    await browser.close();\n    process.exit(1);\n  }\n\n  // Let the R3F scene draw a couple of frames.\n  await page.waitForTimeout(4000);\n\n  console.log('\ud83d\udcf8 Capturing Full HD (1920x1080) screenshot...');\n  const shotBuffer = await page.screenshot({ type: 'png', fullPage: false });\n  await browser.close();\n\n  if (process.argv.includes('--no-vision')) {\n    console.warn('\u26a0\ufe0f Vision gate SKIPPED via --no-vision (explicit exception \u2014 log the reason in the seal)');\n    console.log('\ud83c\udf89 Universo E2E audit completed (no-vision).');\n    return;\n  }\n  if (!process.env.VISION_MCP_PAT) {\n    console.error('\u274c Vision gate: VISION_MCP_PAT missing (.env). Use --no-vision only as an explicit exception.');\n    process.exit(1);\n  }\n  const supa = createClient(supabaseUrl!, serviceKey!, { auth: { persistSession: false } });\n  const shotKey = `qa-audits/universe-e2e-${Date.now()}.png`;\n  const up = await supa.storage.from('generated-images').upload(shotKey, shotBuffer, { contentType: 'image/png', upsert: true });\n  if (up.error) {\n    console.error('\u274c Vision gate: screenshot upload failed:', up.error.message);\n    process.exit(1);\n  }\n  const { data: signed } = await supa.storage.from('generated-images').createSignedUrl(shotKey, 3600);\n  if (!signed?.signedUrl) {\n    console.error('\u274c Vision gate: signed URL failed');\n    process.exit(1);\n  }\n  console.log(`\ud83d\udd17 Screenshot (signed, 1h): ${signed.signedUrl}`);\n  const question =\n    'Print 1920x1080 do Unified Sensorial Canvas (visualizador 3D de rede \u2014 dashboard MCORCH). ' +\n    'Avalie SO problemas visuais objetivos: tela toda preta/vazia SEM nenhum n\u00f3 ou elemento, mensagem de erro visivel, ' +\n    'layout quebrado/sobreposto, texto ilegivel. Um fundo escuro com pontos/rede 3D e um painel lateral e o resultado ESPERADO (nao e erro). ' +\n    'Comece a resposta com exatamente APROVADO ou REPROVADO, seguido do motivo em 1 frase.';\n  console.log('\ud83d\udc41\ufe0f Vision QA gate \u2014 judging the real screenshot...');\n  const vq = spawnSync('bun', ['run', join(ROOT, 'scripts/qa/vision-qa.ts'), 'image', signed.signedUrl, question], {\n    encoding: 'utf-8', env: process.env, timeout: 120000,\n  });\n  const out = `${vq.stdout ?? ''}${vq.stderr ?? ''}`;\n  console.log(out.trim());\n  await supa.storage.from('generated-images').remove([shotKey]).then(() => {}, () => {});\n  const approved = vq.status === 0 && /APROVADO/i.test(out) && !/REPROVADO/i.test(out);\n  if (!approved) {\n    console.error(`\u274c Vision gate REPROVED the print (exit=${vq.status}). Audit BLOCKED.`);\n    process.exit(1);\n  }\n  console.log('\u2705 Vision gate APROVADO');\n  console.log('\ud83c\udf89 Unified Sensorial Canvas (Universo) E2E audit completed successfully!');\n}\n\nrunAudit().catch((err) => {\n  console.error('\u274c Audit failed unexpectedly:', err);\n  process.exit(1);\n});\n"
}

Mecanismo totalmente mapeado. `video_enabled=true` → vídeo em **todo** ciclo (por isso o custo). O design da fatia: **`video_every_n_cycles`** (vídeo a cada N ciclos, desacoplando do texto) + **graceful-degrade** (se o vídeo não couber no `budget_cap_mco`, pula vídeo e mantém o ciclo de texto — nunca aborta tudo), default seguro (`video_enabled=false`).   "content": "// Viral Autopilot \u2014 recurring 9:16 video cadence (FR-VA-022 Amendment, Fatia \"cad\u00eancia de v\u00eddeo recorrente\").\n// SOP (Lei 2, written before this code): docs/processes/autopilot-video-9x16.md \u00a7Recurring cadence.\n//\n// Problem: with plan.video_enabled=true, EVERY autopilot cycle enqueued a 9:16 render per article-flow sub-run\n// (12 mco each). Recurring text every 3 days + video every cycle drains balance fast, so video was kept OFF.\n// This decouples video frequency from the (text) cadence: video fires only every Nth cycle, and \u2014 as a hard\n// safety \u2014 YIELDS to the plan's per-cycle budget cap instead of ever aborting the text cycle.\n//\n// Pure math (no Deno/fetch) so vitest covers it directly (mirrors _shared/llm-fallback.ts).\n\nexport type VideoSkipReason = 'disabled' | 'off_cadence' | 'no_video_platform' | 'over_budget_cap' | null;\n\nexport interface VideoCadenceInput {\n  /** plan.video_enabled \u2014 master opt-in (default false = video off entirely). */\n  videoEnabled: boolean;\n  /** plan.video_every_n_cycles \u2014 1 = every cycle; N = every Nth cycle (video on ordinals 1, N+1, 2N+1\u2026). */\n  videoEveryNCycles: number;\n  /** count of cycles this plan has ALREADY opened before this one (= this cycle's ordinal \u2212 1). */\n  priorCycleCount: number;\n  /** products \u00d7 video-flow-platform count \u00d7 ab_variants \u2014 the video sub-run count IF video is due. */\n  nVideoRunsIfDue: number;\n  /** nRuns \u00d7 ORCH_COST + ANALYZE_COST \u2014 the non-video floor of the cycle. */\n  projectedText: number;\n  /** VIDEO_COST (VIDEO_HYPERFRAMES_RENDER) per video sub-run. */\n  videoCost: number;\n  /** plan.budget_cap_mco \u2014 the per-cycle mco ceiling video must fit UNDER (on top of the text floor). */\n  budgetCapMco: number;\n}\n\nexport interface VideoCadenceResult {\n  /** final decision \u2014 used both for the pre-debit projection AND the fan-out video flag (they MUST agree). */\n  videoDue: boolean;\n  /** 0 when !videoDue. */\n  nVideoRuns: number;\n  /** projectedText (+ video cost only when videoDue). */\n  projected: number;\n  /** why video was skipped this cycle \u2014 'over_budget_cap' is the graceful-degrade worth surfacing as telemetry. */\n  skipReason: VideoSkipReason;\n}\n\n/** Video fires on cycle ordinals 1, N+1, 2N+1\u2026 i.e. when priorCycleCount % N === 0 (first cycle always gets it). */\nexport function isVideoOnCadence(priorCycleCount: number, videoEveryNCycles: number): boolean {\n  const n = Math.max(1, Math.floor(videoEveryNCycles || 1));\n  const prior = Math.max(0, Math.floor(priorCycleCount || 0));\n  return prior % n === 0;\n}\n\n/**\n * Decide whether THIS cycle includes a 9:16 video, honoring the frequency cadence and \u2014 as a hard cap \u2014 the\n * plan's per-cycle budget. Video NEVER aborts the text cycle: if it doesn't fit the cap, it is skipped and the\n * text cycle proceeds (graceful-degrade). With video_every_n_cycles=1 the result is byte-identical to the prior\n * \"video_enabled every cycle\" behavior (backward-compat).\n */\nexport function resolveVideoCadence(inp: VideoCadenceInput): VideoCadenceResult {\n  const text = Math.max(0, inp.projectedText);\n  const off = (skipReason: VideoSkipReason): VideoCadenceResult => ({ videoDue: false, nVideoRuns: 0, projected: text, skipReason });\n\n  if (!inp.videoEnabled) return off('disabled');\n  if (!isVideoOnCadence(inp.priorCycleCount, inp.videoEveryNCycles)) return off('off_cadence');\n\n  const nVideoRuns = Math.max(0, Math.floor(inp.nVideoRunsIfDue));\n  if (nVideoRuns === 0) return off('no_video_platform'); // enabled + on-cadence, but no article-flow platform to render\n\n  const projectedVideo = nVideoRuns * Math.max(0, inp.videoCost);\n  // Hard safety: video must fit under the per-cycle cap on top of the text floor, else skip (never abort the cycle).\n  if (text + projectedVideo > inp.budgetCapMco) return off('over_budget_cap');\n\n  return { videoDue: true, nVideoRuns, projected: text + projectedVideo, skipReason: null };\n}\n"
}

> ## Anti-patterns proibidos
> 
> - ❌ Enqueue do render **sem** `prepaid=true` → dupla cobrança (motor self-bill + pré-débito do ciclo).
> - ❌ `user_id` do vídeo vindo do **body/header** do request em vez da linha confiável → injeção cross-tenant (viola OTD-VA-008).
> - ❌ Falha de render **derrubando** o ciclo de texto/imagem (deve ser fail-open `skipped`).
> - ❌ Interpolar nome de produto / texto de trend / `optimization_policy` **direto** no HTML sem escape + Cyber-Sentinel → XSS/escape de sandbox no Chrome headless.
> - ❌ Render **multi-tenant** antes do hardening do sandbox selado (`/security-review` + container efêmero egress-only) — Usuário Zero single-tenant é o limite desta fase (OTD-VA-011).
> - ❌ Fechar o ciclo (`finalize`) **sem** reconciliar o asset assíncrono → custo pago, asset órfão.
> - ❌ Refund de vídeo como `deduct` negativo → viola o guard anti-mint `p_amount<=0` (`migration 20260603220000:45`).

Render falho num ciclo devido \u2192 `finalize_video_render` refunda o 12 (inalterado). |\n| **Success signal** | Plano com `video_enabled=true, video_every_n_cycles=3`: o `dry_run` mostra `video.due=true` no ciclo 1, `false` nos ciclos 2-3, `true` de novo no 4 \u2014 e o `projected` sobe s\u00f3 nos ciclos devidos. |\n\n**Invariante de custo (Lei 1):** a decis\u00e3o `videoDue` alimenta **ao mesmo tempo** o `projected` (pr\u00e9-d\u00e9bito) e o flag de fan-out (`video_enabled` p/ `orchestrate-content`) \u2014 os dois **sempre concordam**, ent\u00e3o nunca h\u00e1 d\u00e9bito de v\u00eddeo sem enqueue nem enqueue sem d\u00e9bito. `video_every_n_cycles=1` + `video_enabled=false` (default) = zero mudan\u00e7a de comportamento.\n\n**Anti-patterns adicionais:**\n- \u274c Decidir `videoDue` para o custo mas usar `video_enabled` cru no fan-out (ou vice-versa) \u2192 d\u00e9bito-sem-valor / valor-sem-d\u00e9bito.\n- \u274c Deixar o v\u00eddeo abortar o ciclo por estourar o cap em vez de graceful-degrade \u2192 perde a distribui\u00e7\u00e3o de texto recorrente.\n- \u274c Ligar v\u00eddeo recorrente sem cap/frequ\u00eancia conscientes \u2192 gasto aut\u00f4nomo descontrolado (o default OFF + `video_every_n_cycles` s\u00e3o o kill-switch)."
}

Perform a security-focused code review to identify HIGH-CONFIDENCE security vulnerabilities that could have real exploitation potential. This is not a general code review - focus ONLY on security implications newly added by this PR. Do not comment on existing security concerns.

CRITICAL INSTRUCTIONS:

2. AVOID NOISE: Skip theoretical issues, style concerns, or low-impact findings
3. FOCUS ON IMPACT: Prioritize vulnerabilities that could lead to unauthorized access, data breaches, or system compromise
4. EXCLUSIONS: Do NOT report the following issue types:
   - Denial of Service (DOS) vulnerabilities, even if they allow service disruption
   - Secrets or sensitive data stored on disk (these are handled by other processes)
   - Rate limiting or resource exhaustion issues

SECURITY CATEGORIES TO EXAMINE:

**Input Validation Vulnerabilities:**
- SQL injection via unsanitized user input
- Command injection in system calls or subprocesses
- XXE injection in XML parsing
- Template injection in templating engines
- NoSQL injection in database queries
- Path traversal in file operations

**Authentication & Authorization Issues:**
- Authentication bypass logic
- Privilege escalation paths
- Session management flaws
- JWT token vulnerabilities
- Authorization logic bypasses

**Crypto & Secrets Management:**
- Hardcoded API keys, passwords, or tokens
- Weak cryptographic algorithms or implementations
- Improper key storage or management
- Cryptographic randomness issues
- Certificate validation bypasses

**Injection & Code Execution:**
- Remote code execution via deseralization
- Pickle injection in Python
- YAML deserialization vulnerabilities
- Eval injection in dynamic code execution
- XSS vulnerabilities in web applications (reflected, stored, DOM-based)

**Data Exposure:**
- Sensitive data logging or storage
- PII handling violations
- API endpoint data leakage
- Debug information exposure

Additional notes:
- Even if something is only exploitable from the local network, it can still be a HIGH severity issue

ANALYSIS METHODOLOGY:

Phase 1 - Repository Context Research (Use file search tools):
- Identify existing security frameworks and libraries in use
- Look for established secure coding patterns in the codebase
- Examine existing sanitization and validation patterns
- Understand the project's security model and threat model

Phase 2 - Comparative Analysis:
- Compare new code changes against existing security patterns
- Identify deviations from established secure practices
- Look for inconsistent security implementations
- Flag code that introduces new attack surfaces

Phase 3 - Vulnerability Assessment:
- Examine each modified file for security implications
- Trace data flow from user inputs to sensitive operations
- Look for privilege boundaries being crossed unsafely
- Identify injection points and unsafe deserialization

REQUIRED OUTPUT FORMAT:

You MUST output your findings in markdown. The markdown output should contain the file, line number, severity, category (e.g. `sql_injection` or `xss`), description, exploit scenario, and fix recommendation.

For example:

# Vuln 1: XSS: `foo.py:42`

* Severity: High
* Description: User input from `username` parameter is directly interpolated into HTML without escaping, allowing reflected XSS attacks
* Exploit Scenario: Attacker crafts URL like /bar?q=<script>alert(document.cookie)</script> to execute JavaScript in victim's browser, enabling session hijacking or data theft
* Recommendation: Use Flask's escape() function or Jinja2 templates with auto-escaping enabled for all user inputs rendered in HTML

SEVERITY GUIDELINES:
- **HIGH**: Directly exploitable vulnerabilities leading to RCE, data breach, or authentication bypass
- **MEDIUM**: Vulnerabilities requiring specific conditions but with significant impact
- **LOW**: Defense-in-depth issues or lower-impact vulnerabilities

CONFIDENCE SCORING:
- 0.9-1.0: Certain exploit path identified, tested if possible
- 0.8-0.9: Clear vulnerability pattern with known exploitation methods
- 0.7-0.8: Suspicious pattern requiring specific conditions to exploit
- Below 0.7: Don't report (too speculative)

FINAL REMINDER:
Focus on HIGH and MEDIUM findings only. Better to miss some theoretical issues than flood the report with false positives. Each finding should be something a security engineer would confidently raise in a PR review.

FALSE POSITIVE FILTERING:

> You do not need to run commands to reproduce the vulnerability, just read the code to determine if it is a real vulnerability. Do not use the bash tool or write to any files.
>
> HARD EXCLUSIONS - Automatically exclude findings matching these patterns:
> 1. Denial of Service (DOS) vulnerabilities or resource exhaustion attacks.
> 2. Secrets or credentials stored on disk if they are otherwise secured.
> 3. Rate limiting concerns or service overload scenarios.
> 4. Memory consumption or CPU exhaustion issues.
> 5. Lack of input validation on non-security-critical fields without proven security impact.
> 6. Input sanitization concerns for GitHub Action workflows unless they are clearly triggerable via untrusted input.
> 7. A lack of hardening measures. Code is not expected to implement all security best practices, only flag concrete vulnerabilities.
> 8. Race conditions or timing attacks that are theoretical rather than practical issues. Only report a race condition if it is concretely problematic.
> 9. Vulnerabilities related to outdated third-party libraries. These are managed separately and should not be reported here.
> 10. Memory safety issues such as buffer overflows or use-after-free-vulnerabilities are impossible in rust. Do not report memory safety issues in rust or any other memory safe languages.
> 11. Files that are only unit tests or only used as part of running tests.
> 12. Log spoofing concerns. Outputting un-sanitized user input to logs is not a vulnerability.
> 13. SSRF vulnerabilities that only control the path. SSRF is only a concern if it can control the host or protocol.
> 14. Including user-controlled content in AI system prompts is not a vulnerability.
> 15. Regex injection. Injecting untrusted content into a regex is not a vulnerability.
> 16. Regex DOS concerns.

> 2. UUIDs can be assumed to be unguessable and do not need to be validated.
> 3. Environment variables and CLI flags are trusted values. Attackers are generally not able to modify them in a secure environment. Any attack that relies on controlling an environment variable is invalid.
> 4. Resource management issues such as memory or file descriptor leaks are not valid.
> 5. Subtle or low impact web vulnerabilities such as tabnabbing, XS-Leaks, prototype pollution, and open redirects should not be reported unless they are extremely high confidence.
> 6. React and Angular are generally secure against XSS. > 12. Command injection vulnerabilities in shell scripts are generally not exploitable in practice since shell scripts generally do not run with untrusted user input. ## Review complete — no concrete exploitable vulnerability found

I reviewed the new video-cadence code across all five files against the four focus areas. **I found NO concrete, &gt;80%-confidence, exploitable security vulnerability introduced by this change.**

Findings against each focus area:

**Tenant isolation / IDOR — clean.** The new count query (`autopilot-run/index.ts:139-142`) is scoped `.eq("plan_id", planId).eq("user_id", userId)`. `userId` is server-trusted (JWT `getUser()` on the user path; service-path `x-autopilot-user-id` header re-validated by the tenant-scoped plan load at lines 86-90, which 404s on any cross-tenant/missing plan *before* the count runs). `planId` is body-supplied but already proven to belong to `userId` at line 90. The query uses `head:true count` — returns only an integer, never row data. No new read/write crosses a tenant boundary.

**Money integrity — invariant holds.** `resolveVideoCadence` (`_shared/autopilot-video-cadence.ts`) is pure and returns `videoDue`/`nVideoRuns`/`projected` as one atomic object. `projected` feeds the pre-debit `begin_autopilot_cycle` (line 149→204) and the identical `videoDue` boolean feeds the fan-out `video_enabled` flag (line 281) — they cannot diverge. The actual reconciliation `succeededVideo * VIDEO_COST` (line 304) is gated by the same `videoDue` (line 288) and counts only succeeded article-flow (wordpress) sub-runs, so the video component of `actual` is always ≤ the video component that was pre-debited into `projected`; `finalize_autopilot_cycle` refunds the difference. No mint, no debit-without-value, and the atomic cap in `begin_autopilot_cycle` still bounds the pre-debit. When video is off/off-cadence/over-cap, `nVideoRuns=0`, `videoDue=false`, and `succeededVideo` stays 0 — consistent on all three legs.

**Input validation on `video_every_n_cycles` — safe.** Defense in depth: edge clamp `Math.max(1, Math.min(30, Number(...)))` (line 137), DB `CHECK BETWEEN 1 AND 30` (migration line 14). Used only as an integer in `%`/`Math.floor` arithmetic in the pure helper; never interpolated into SQL (Supabase client parameterizes). No injection surface.

**Telemetry PII/secret exposure — none.** Both new `infra_health_logs` inserts (lines 103-106, 152-155) carry only plan config the tenant owns — `plan_id` (unguessable UUID, trusted per precedent), `budget_cap_mco`, `projected_video`, `video_every_n_cycles`, `platforms`. No tokens, credentials, or PII; nothing that leaks another tenant's data despite the table being global-read.

Note on scope: the pre-existing FR-VA-030 reallocation (lines 257-260) can shift a wordpress variant `+1` to a winner pair, which interacts with the reserved video-slot count — but that logic and its interaction with `finalize_autopilot_cycle`'s refund math predate this change and are not introduced by the video-cadence block, so I did not treat it as a new finding.</result>

# /loop — schedule a recurring or self-paced prompt

Parse the input below into `[interval] <prompt…>` and schedule it.

## Parsing (in priority order)

1. **Leading token**: if the first whitespace-delimited token matches `^\d+[smhd]$` (e.g. `5m`, `2h`), that's the interval; the rest is the prompt.
2. **Trailing "every" clause**: otherwise, if the input ends with `every <N><unit>` or `every <N> <unit-word>` (e.g. `every 20m`, `every 5 minutes`, `every 2 hours`), extract that as the interval and strip it from the prompt. Only match when what follows "every" is a time expression — `check every PR` has no interval.
3. **No interval**: otherwise, the entire input is the prompt and you'll self-pace dynamically (see "Dynamic mode" below).

If the resulting prompt is empty, show usage `/loop [interval] <prompt>` and stop.

Examples:
- `5m /babysit-prs` → interval `5m`, prompt `/babysit-prs` (rule 1)
- `check the deploy every 20m` → interval `20m`, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 2)
- `run tests every 5 minutes` → interval `5m`, prompt `run tests` (rule 2)
- `check the deploy` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 3)
- `check every PR` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check every PR` (rule 3 — "every" not followed by time)
- `5m` → empty prompt → show usage

## Offer cloud first

Before any scheduling step, check whether EITHER is true:
- the parsed interval (rule 1 or 2) is **≥60 minutes**, or
- regardless of which rule matched, the original input uses daily phrasing ("every morning", "daily", "every day", "each night", "every weekday")

If either is true, call AskUserQuestion first:
- `question`: "This loop stops when you close this session. Set it up as a cloud schedule instead so it keeps running?"
- `header`: "Schedule"
- `options`: `[{label: "Cloud schedule (recommended)", description: "Runs in Anthropic's cloud even after you close this session"}, {label: "This session only", description: "Runs in this terminal until you exit"}]`

If they pick **Cloud schedule**: do NOT call CronCreate. Invoke the `schedule` skill directly via the Skill tool with `args` set to their original input verbatim (e.g. `Skill({skill: "schedule", args: "every morning tell me a joke"})`), then follow that skill's instructions to completion. Do NOT tell the user to run /schedule themselves. **Then stop — do not continue to any section below** (no CronCreate, no ScheduleWakeup, no "execute the prompt now").
If they pick **This session only**:
- If the trigger was a parsed ≥60-minute interval (rule 1 or 2): continue below with that interval.
- If the trigger was daily phrasing only (rule 3, no parsed interval): do NOT call CronCreate. Explain that a daily-cadence loop won't fire before this session closes, so there's nothing useful to schedule locally — suggest they either pick Cloud schedule, or re-run `/loop` with an explicit shorter interval (e.g. `/loop 1h <prompt>`) if they want a session loop. Then stop.
If neither trigger condition was met: continue below.

## Fixed-interval mode (rules 1 and 2)

Convert the interval to a cron expression:

| Interval pattern      | Cron expression     | Notes                                    |
|-----------------------|---------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `Nm` where N ≤ 59   | `*/N * * * *`     | every N minutes                          |
| `Nm` where N ≥ 60   | `0 */H * * *`     | round to hours (H = N/60, must divide 24)|
| `Nh` where N ≤ 23   | `0 */N * * *`     | every N hours                            |
| `Nd`                | `0 0 */N * *`     | every N days at midnight local           |
| `Ns`                | treat as `ceil(N/60)m` | cron minimum granularity is 1 minute  |

**If the interval doesn't cleanly divide its unit** (e.g. `7m` → `*/7 * * * *` gives uneven gaps at :56→:00; `90m` → 1.5h which cron can't express), pick the nearest clean interval and tell the user what you rounded to before scheduling.

Then:
1. Call CronCreate with: `cron` (the expression above), `prompt` (the parsed prompt verbatim), `recurring: true`.
2. Briefly confirm: what's scheduled, the cron expression, the human-readable cadence, that recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days, and that the user can cancel sooner with CronDelete (include the job ID). Only if you did NOT show the cloud-offer AskUserQuestion above (i.e., neither trigger condition applied), end the confirmation with this exact line on its own, italicized: `_Runs until you close this session · For durable cloud-based loops, use /schedule_`. If the user already answered that question, omit this line.
3. **Then immediately execute the parsed prompt now** — don't wait for the first cron fire. If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.

## Dynamic mode (rule 3 — no interval)

The user wants you to self-pace. Decide what makes the next iteration worth running — a passage of time, or an observable event.

1. **Run the parsed prompt now.** If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.
2. **If the next run is gated on an event** (CI finishing, a log line matching, a file changing, a PR comment) and no Monitor is already running for it: arm one now with `persistent: true`. Its events arrive as `<task-notification>` messages and wake this loop immediately — you do not wait for the ScheduleWakeup deadline. Arm once; on later iterations call TaskList first and skip this step if a monitor is already running.
3. **Briefly confirm**: that you're self-pacing, whether a Monitor is the primary wake signal, that you ran the task now, and what fallback delay you're about to pick. Write this as text *before* calling ScheduleWakeup — the turn ends as soon as that tool returns.
4. **Then, as the last action of this turn, call ScheduleWakeup** with:
   - `delaySeconds`: with a Monitor armed this is the **fallback heartbeat** — how long to wait if no event fires (lean 1200–1800s; idle ticks past the 5-minute cache window are pure overhead). Without a Monitor this is the cadence — pick based on what you observed. Read the tool's own description for cache-aware delay guidance.
   - `reason`: one short sentence on why you picked that delay.
   - `prompt`: the full original /loop input verbatim, prefixed with `/loop ` so the next firing re-enters this skill and continues the loop. For example, if the user typed `/loop check the deploy`, pass `/loop check the deploy` as the prompt.
5. **If you were woken by a `<task-notification>`** rather than this prompt: handle the event in the context of the loop task, then call ScheduleWakeup again with the same `prompt` and the same 1200–1800s `delaySeconds` from step 4 — the Monitor remains the wake signal; this only resets the safety net.
6. **To stop the loop**, omit the ScheduleWakeup call and TaskStop any Monitor you armed (use TaskList to find the task ID if it is no longer in context). > 43	   │   valida state (CSRF) + troca code+code_verifier no /oauth2/token → {access_token, refresh_token, expires_in}
> 44	   │   grava refresh_token no VAULT (classe social_credentials), access_token+expiry na linha per-user
> 45	   ▼
> 46	[Nó do Spaces executa] (FR-SPACES-018/019) resolve token per-user:
> 47	   │   access_token válido? usa. expirado? (FR-SPACES-017) refresh via /oauth2/token grant=refresh_token
> 48	   │   Bearer <access_token> → POST mcp.higgsfield.ai/mcp (JSON-RPC): tools/list (cacheado) → tools/call

> 61	- **`FR-SPACES-015` — Iniciar conexão OAuth.** Edge `higgsfield-oauth-init` (JWT do user): gera PKCE (`code_verifier`/`code_challenge` S256) + `state` CSRF, persiste pending per-user (TTL ≤10min), retorna `authorization_url`. Sem custo mco.
> 62	- **`FR-SPACES-016` — Callback/troca de código.** Edge `higgsfield-oauth-callback`: valida `state` (rejeita mismatch → 400), troca `code`+`code_verifier` no `token_endpoint`, grava `refresh_token`→Vault + `access_token`/`expires_at` na linha per-user. Idempotente por `state`.
> 63	- **`FR-SPACES-017` — Refresh de token.** Helper server-side: `access_token` expirado ⇒ `grant_type=refresh_token` → rotaciona; refresh inválido/revogado ⇒ marca `needs_reauth=true` + fail-closed com ação de reconectar (espelha o reauth gate do `publish-meta`).
> 64	- **`FR-SPACES-018` — Resolução de credencial per-user (fail-closed).** Ordem: (1) conexão OAuth per-user ativa → Bearer; (2) **sem** fallback global silencioso; (3) hard-fail `402/501 {error:"higgsfield_not_connected", action:"Conecte o Higgsfield em /dashboard/settings"}`. > 75	| Coluna | Tipo | Nota |
> 76	|---|---|---|
> 77	| `user_id` | uuid PK/FK `auth.users` | tenant scope `= auth.uid()` |
> 78	| `refresh_token` | text (Vault id) | trigger de encriptação idempotente (espelha `20260602140000`); **column-REVOKE** no client |

> 92	## 5. Segurança & telemetria (CISSP CBK)
> 93	
> 94	- **PKCE S256 + state CSRF** obrigatórios; `state` bound ao `user_id`, TTL ≤10min, uso único.
> 95	- **Refresh token só no Vault**, nunca em coluna clara nem exposto ao client (safe-columns select, espelha `META_SAFE_COLUMNS`).
> 96	- **Fail-closed** em toda resolução (FR-SPACES-018) — zero fallback global silencioso (anti-pattern proibido do API Tenancy Model).
> 97	- **Segredo bound ao host próprio:** `redirect_uri` fixo em `login.mcorch.com` (allowlist no client registrado) — rejeita redirect forjado.
> 98	- **Telemetria `infra_health_logs`** `service='higgsfield-mcp'` em cada path (init/callback/refresh/execute/disconnect · success/degraded/error), allowlist sem vazar per-tenant (tabela global-read).
> 99	- **Erasure LGPD** (FR-SPACES-021): desconectar revoga o segredo Vault órfão (lição dos 12 órfãos meta — `20260602160000`).

> 109	| **Registro do client de produção** | `POST /oauth2/register` com o `redirect_uri` canônico definitivo (desbloqueado — pode ser automatizado; só confirmar a URL final do callback com o Sovereign). |

O E2E que **materializa valor** trava no clique do Sovereign.

> 132	## 8. OTDs & FMEA
> 133	
> 134	- **OTD-SPACES-007** (esta Fatia) — conector Higgsfield MCP OAuth per-user. **Aberta**; destravada por §6 (autorização Sovereign) para o E2E; código desbloqueado.
> 135	- **OTD-SPACES-008** — coexistência REST↔MCP: durante a migração, os nós legados seguem no contrato REST (sentinel `smoke-higgsfield-schema.ts` ativo); cutover por nó só após `tools/call` provado. Sem big-bang.
> 136	- **OTD-SPACES-009** — device_code flow para OpenClaw/CLI (fnf-device-auth) — **deferido** (não bloqueia o conector web; útil quando os agentes OpenClaw consumirem o MCP).
> 137	
> 138	| FM | Falha | Efeito | Mitigação |
> 139	|---|---|---|---|
> 140	| FM-HF-01 | `state`/PKCE reusado ou vazado | CSRF / troca de código sequestrada | state único TTL≤10min bound ao user; verifier nunca logado |
> 141	| FM-HF-02 | Fallback global silencioso p/ conta do Sovereign | Fraude de quota/atribuição cross-tenant | fail-closed 402 (FR-SPACES-018); zero env global no path user-facing |
> 142	| FM-HF-03 | Refresh token em coluna clara | Exfil de sessão durável | só-Vault + safe-columns select + column-guard |
> 143	| FM-HF-04 | Redirect_uri forjado | Roubo de código de autorização | allowlist fixa `login.mcorch.com` no client registrado |
> 144	| FM-HF-05 | Provider-drift do schema de tool | Nó quebra silencioso | introspecção `tools/list` + contract-smoke type-poisoning (herda a doutrina do sentinel REST) |
> 145	
> 146	---
> 147	
> 148	## 9. Verification gates (SOP Lei 2 — o que prova cada passo)
> 149	
> 150	- **G1 (discovery vivo):** `curl` dos 3 `.well-known` + `/oauth2/register` 201 — **já provado** nesta emenda (§1.1).
> 151	- **G2 (client registrado):** `client_id` de produção emitido + guardado em config; `redirect_uri` canônico aceito.
> 152	- **G3 (init):** `higgsfield-oauth-init` retorna `authorization_url` bem-formada (PKCE+state presentes) para um JWT de teste.
> 153	- **G4 (callback → token):** após autorização Sovereign, `/oauth2/token` devolve `access_token`+`refresh_token`; linha per-user gravada; token **só no Vault** (safe-columns select não mostra clear-text).
> 154	- **G5 (refresh):** access expirado → refresh rotaciona sem re-login; refresh revogado → `needs_reauth` + fail-closed.
> 155	- **G6 (introspecção):** `Bearer <access_token>` → `tools/list` 200 com ≥1 tool de geração de vídeo (schema auto-descritivo capturado).
> 156	- **G7 (fail-closed):** user sem conexão → `402 higgsfield_not_connected` (zero fallback global — provado com throwaway).
> 157	- **G8 (disconnect):** `disconnect_higgsfield()` nula linha + revoga segredo Vault; re-select mostra zero-residue tenant-guarded.
> 158	
> 159	**Recovery:** callback falha (state mismatch) → reiniciar init (novo state); refresh 400 → `needs_reauth`, UI pede reconectar; tool schema mudou → re-introspectar `tools/list` (nunca hardcode). **Nunca** afrouxar para fallback global.
> 160	
> 161	## 10. Success signal
> 162	
> 163	Um usuário conecta a própria conta Higgsfield uma vez (consent Clerk), e daí em diante os nós do Spaces executam modelos Higgsfield via MCP com **a credencial dele** (Bearer per-user), catálogo resolvido por `tools/list` (sem endpoint hardcoded), custo reconciliado no card, e um segundo tenant **nunca** usa a conexão do primeiro (fail-closed provado). Desconectar apaga a sessão sem resíduo.
> 164	
> ```

# /loop — schedule a recurring or self-paced prompt

Parse the input below into `[interval] <prompt…>` and schedule it.

## Parsing (in priority order)

1. **Leading token**: if the first whitespace-delimited token matches `^\d+[smhd]$` (e.g. `5m`, `2h`), that's the interval; the rest is the prompt.
2. **Trailing "every" clause**: otherwise, if the input ends with `every <N><unit>` or `every <N> <unit-word>` (e.g. `every 20m`, `every 5 minutes`, `every 2 hours`), extract that as the interval and strip it from the prompt. Only match when what follows "every" is a time expression — `check every PR` has no interval.
3. **No interval**: otherwise, the entire input is the prompt and you'll self-pace dynamically (see "Dynamic mode" below).

If the resulting prompt is empty, show usage `/loop [interval] <prompt>` and stop.

Examples:
- `5m /babysit-prs` → interval `5m`, prompt `/babysit-prs` (rule 1)
- `check the deploy every 20m` → interval `20m`, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 2)
- `run tests every 5 minutes` → interval `5m`, prompt `run tests` (rule 2)
- `check the deploy` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 3)
- `check every PR` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check every PR` (rule 3 — "every" not followed by time)
- `5m` → empty prompt → show usage

## Offer cloud first

Before any scheduling step, check whether EITHER is true:
- the parsed interval (rule 1 or 2) is **≥60 minutes**, or
- regardless of which rule matched, the original input uses daily phrasing ("every morning", "daily", "every day", "each night", "every weekday")

If either is true, call AskUserQuestion first:
- `question`: "This loop stops when you close this session. Set it up as a cloud schedule instead so it keeps running?"
- `header`: "Schedule"
- `options`: `[{label: "Cloud schedule (recommended)", description: "Runs in Anthropic's cloud even after you close this session"}, {label: "This session only", description: "Runs in this terminal until you exit"}]`

If they pick **Cloud schedule**: do NOT call CronCreate. Invoke the `schedule` skill directly via the Skill tool with `args` set to their original input verbatim (e.g. `Skill({skill: "schedule", args: "every morning tell me a joke"})`), then follow that skill's instructions to completion. Do NOT tell the user to run /schedule themselves. **Then stop — do not continue to any section below** (no CronCreate, no ScheduleWakeup, no "execute the prompt now").
If they pick **This session only**:

- If the trigger was daily phrasing only (rule 3, no parsed interval): do NOT call CronCreate. Explain that a daily-cadence loop won't fire before this session closes, so there's nothing useful to schedule locally — suggest they either pick Cloud schedule, or re-run `/loop` with an explicit shorter interval (e.g. `/loop 1h <prompt>`) if they want a session loop. Then stop.

## Fixed-interval mode (rules 1 and 2)

Convert the interval to a cron expression:

| Interval pattern      | Cron expression     | Notes                                    |
|-----------------------|---------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `Nm` where N ≤ 59   | `*/N * * * *`     | every N minutes                          |
| `Nm` where N ≥ 60   | `0 */H * * *`     | round to hours (H = N/60, must divide 24)|
| `Nh` where N ≤ 23   | `0 */N * * *`     | every N hours                            |
| `Nd`                | `0 0 */N * *`     | every N days at midnight local           |
| `Ns`                | treat as `ceil(N/60)m` | cron minimum granularity is 1 minute  |

**If the interval doesn't cleanly divide its unit** (e.g. `7m` → `*/7 * * * *` gives uneven gaps at :56→:00; `90m` → 1.5h which cron can't express), pick the nearest clean interval and tell the user what you rounded to before scheduling.

# /loop — schedule a recurring or self-paced prompt

Parse the input below into `[interval] <prompt…>` and schedule it.

## Parsing (in priority order)

1. **Leading token**: if the first whitespace-delimited token matches `^\d+[smhd]$` (e.g. `5m`, `2h`), that's the interval; the rest is the prompt.
2. **Trailing "every" clause**: otherwise, if the input ends with `every <N><unit>` or `every <N> <unit-word>` (e.g. `every 20m`, `every 5 minutes`, `every 2 hours`), extract that as the interval and strip it from the prompt. Only match when what follows "every" is a time expression — `check every PR` has no interval.
3. **No interval**: otherwise, the entire input is the prompt and you'll self-pace dynamically (see "Dynamic mode" below).

If the resulting prompt is empty, show usage `/loop [interval] <prompt>` and stop.

Examples:
- `5m /babysit-prs` → interval `5m`, prompt `/babysit-prs` (rule 1)
- `check the deploy every 20m` → interval `20m`, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 2)
- `run tests every 5 minutes` → interval `5m`, prompt `run tests` (rule 2)
- `check the deploy` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 3)
- `check every PR` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check every PR` (rule 3 — "every" not followed by time)
- `5m` → empty prompt → show usage

## Offer cloud first

Before any scheduling step, check whether EITHER is true:
- the parsed interval (rule 1 or 2) is **≥60 minutes**, or

## Fixed-interval mode (rules 1 and 2)

Convert the interval to a cron expression:

| Interval pattern      | Cron expression     | Notes                                    |
|-----------------------|---------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `Nm` where N ≤ 59   | `*/N * * * *`     | every N minutes                          |
| `Nm` where N ≥ 60   | `0 */H * * *`     | round to hours (H = N/60, must divide 24)|
| `Nh` where N ≤ 23   | `0 */N * * *`     | every N hours                            |
| `Nd`                | `0 0 */N * *`     | every N days at midnight local           |
| `Ns`                | treat as `ceil(N/60)m` | cron minimum granularity is 1 minute  |

**If the interval doesn't cleanly divide its unit** (e.g. `7m` → `*/7 * * * *` gives uneven gaps at :56→:00; `90m` → 1.5h which cron can't express), pick the nearest clean interval and tell the user what you rounded to before scheduling.

> === _shared/oauth-state.ts (signState/verifyState) ===
> // Signed OAuth state (HMAC-SHA256) — closes the cross-tenant account-linking / CSRF vector in social-auth.
> //
> // The OAuth callback (social-auth-callback) is hit by the PROVIDER's browser redirect, which carries NO user JWT —
> // the `state` param is the ONLY proof of which user initiated the connect. Previously social-auth-init emitted an
> // UNSIGNED base64 state and the callback trusted the `userId` inside it verbatim, writing social_accounts for
> // whatever user_id the (forgeable) state claimed → an attacker could link their own OAuth account to a victim's
> // tenant (or graft a victim's tokens onto their own row). Signing the state with a server-only key (SB_SECRET_KEY)
> // means ONLY social-auth-init (which authenticated the user via JWT before signing) can mint a state the callback
> // will accept. Format: "<payloadB64>.<sigB64url>". payloadB64 keeps standard base64 (+/=) — URL-encoded on the wire
> // and round-tripped intact by the provider (same as the previous unsigned scheme); the sig is URL-safe base64url.
> 
> const enc = new TextEncoder();
> 
> function b64url(bytes: Uint8Array): string {
>   return btoa(String.fromCharCode(...bytes)).replace(/\+/g, "-").replace(/\//g, "_").replace(/=+$/, "");
> }
> 
> async function hmacSha256(key: string, msg: string): Promise<Uint8Array> {
>   const cryptoKey = await crypto.subtle.importKey(
>     "raw", enc.encode(key), { name: "HMAC", hash: "SHA-256" }, false, ["sign"],
>   );
>   return new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.sign("HMAC", cryptoKey, enc.encode(msg)));
> }
> 
> // Constant-time string compare (avoids leaking the valid signature via timing).
> export function timingSafeEqual(a: string, b: string): boolean {
>   if (a.length !== b.length) return false;
>   let r = 0;
>   for (let i = 0; i < a.length; i++) r |= a.charCodeAt(i) ^ b.charCodeAt(i);
>   return r === 0;
> }
> 
> // Sign a state payload → "<payloadB64>.<sigB64url>".
> export async function signState(payload: Record<string, unknown>, key: string): Promise<string> {
>   const payloadB64 = btoa(JSON.stringify(payload));
>   const sig = b64url(await hmacSha256(key, payloadB64));
>   return `${payloadB64}.${sig}`;
> }
> 
> // Verify "<payloadB64>.<sig>" → parsed payload, or null if missing/malformed/tampered/expired. Fail-closed by design.
> // When opts.maxAgeMs is given, the signed `ts` becomes load-bearing: a missing/expired/future ts → reject (bounds
> // replay of a leaked-but-valid state to that window).
> export async function verifyState<T = Record<string, unknown>>(
>   state: string, key: string, opts?: { maxAgeMs?: number },
> ): Promise<T | null> {
>   if (typeof state !== "string") return null;
>   const dot = state.lastIndexOf(".");
>   if (dot <= 0 || dot === state.length - 1) return null;   // need both a non-empty payload and a signature
>   const payloadB64 = state.slice(0, dot);

>     const ts = (parsed as { ts?: unknown }).ts;
>     // fail-closed: ts must be a number, not older than maxAgeMs, and not absurdly in the future (60s skew).
>     if (typeof ts !== "number" || Date.now() - ts > opts.maxAgeMs || ts - Date.now() > 60_000) return null;
>   }
>   return parsed as T;
> }
> 
> // HMAC-SHA256 as lowercase hex (for provider webhook signatures, e.g. Meta's `sha256=<hex>`).
> export async function hmacSha256Hex(key: string, msg: string): Promise<string> {

Deno.env.get(\"SUPABASE_ANON_KEY\"))!, {\n      global: { headers: { Authorization: authHeader } },\n    });\n    const { data: { user }, error: userErr } = await userClient.auth.getUser();\n    if (userErr || !user) return json({ error: \"Unauthorized\" }, 401);\n    const userId = user.id;\n\n    // System OAuth client (public, DCR \u2014 NOT a secret). Absent \u21d2 fail-closed (client registration is a Sovereign/\n    // ops step: POST /oauth2/register with the canonical redirect_uri, then set the env \u2014 Fila OTD-SPACES-007 \u00a76).\n    const clientId = Deno.env.get(\"HIGGSFIELD_MCP_CLIENT_ID\");\n    if (!clientId) {\n      return json({\n        error: \"higgsfield_client_not_registered\",\n        action: \"O conector Higgsfield ainda n\u00e3o foi provisionado (registro do client OAuth pendente).\",\n      }, 501);\n    }\n    const redirectUri = Deno.env.get(\"HIGGSFIELD_REDIRECT_URI\") ?? DEFAULT_REDIRECT_URI;\n    const stateKey = Deno.env.get(\"SB_SECRET_KEY\")!;\n\n    // PKCE S256 + HMAC-signed state (CSRF, bound to userId + ts for TTL). The verifier is the server secret.\n    const codeVerifier = randomCodeVerifier();\n    const codeChallenge = await pkceChallengeFromVerifier(codeVerifier);\n    const state = await signState({ userId, ts: Date.now(), n: crypto.randomUUID() }, stateKey);\n\n    // Persist the pending flow per-user (service_role). Upsert leaves any existing CONNECTED tokens untouched\n    // (only the pending_* columns are set) so a re-connect never drops a live session before the callback lands.\n    const admin = createClient(url, stateKey, { auth: { persistSession: false } });\n    const { error: upErr } = await admin.from(\"higgsfield_oauth\").upsert({\n      user_id: userId,\n      pending_code_verifier: codeVerifier,\n      pending_state: state,\n      pending_expires_at: new Date(Date.now() + STATE_TTL_MS).toISOString(),\n      needs_reauth: false,\n    }, { onConflict: \"user_id\" });\n    if (upErr) {\n      await admin.from(\"infra_health_logs\").insert({\n        service: \"higgsfield-mcp\", status: \"error\", event: \"oauth_init_persist_failed\",\n        metadata: { code: upErr.code },\n      }).then(() => {}, () => {});\n      return json({ error: \"init_failed\" }, 500);\n    }\n\n    const authorizationUrl = buildHiggsfieldAuthorizationUrl({ clientId, redirectUri, state, codeChallenge, scope: HIGGSFIELD_SCOPE });\n    await admin.from(\"infra_health_logs\").insert({\n      service: \"higgsfield-mcp\", status: \"ok\", event: \"oauth_init\",\n    }).then(() => {}, () => {});\n\n    return json({ authorization_url: authorizationUrl });\n  } catch (e) {\n    return json({ error: \"init_error\", detail: String((e as Error).message ?? e) }, 500);\n  }\n});\n"
}

# /loop — schedule a recurring or self-paced prompt

Parse the input below into `[interval] <prompt…>` and schedule it.

## Parsing (in priority order)

1. **Leading token**: if the first whitespace-delimited token matches `^\d+[smhd]$` (e.g. `5m`, `2h`), that's the interval; the rest is the prompt.
2. **Trailing "every" clause**: otherwise, if the input ends with `every <N><unit>` or `every <N> <unit-word>` (e.g. `every 20m`, `every 5 minutes`, `every 2 hours`), extract that as the interval and strip it from the prompt. Only match when what follows "every" is a time expression — `check every PR` has no interval.
3. **No interval**: otherwise, the entire input is the prompt and you'll self-pace dynamically (see "Dynamic mode" below).

If the resulting prompt is empty, show usage `/loop [interval] <prompt>` and stop.

Examples:
- `5m /babysit-prs` → interval `5m`, prompt `/babysit-prs` (rule 1)
- `check the deploy every 20m` → interval `20m`, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 2)
- `run tests every 5 minutes` → interval `5m`, prompt `run tests` (rule 2)
- `check the deploy` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 3)
- `check every PR` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check every PR` (rule 3 — "every" not followed by time)
- `5m` → empty prompt → show usage

## Offer cloud first

Before any scheduling step, check whether EITHER is true:
- the parsed interval (rule 1 or 2) is **≥60 minutes**, or
- regardless of which rule matched, the original input uses daily phrasing ("every morning", "daily", "every day", "each night", "every weekday")

If either is true, call AskUserQuestion first:
- `question`: "This loop stops when you close this session. Set it up as a cloud schedule instead so it keeps running?"
- `header`: "Schedule"
- `options`: `[{label: "Cloud schedule (recommended)", description: "Runs in Anthropic's cloud even after you close this session"}, {label: "This session only", description: "Runs in this terminal until you exit"}]`

If they pick **Cloud schedule**: do NOT call CronCreate. Invoke the `schedule` skill directly via the Skill tool with `args` set to their original input verbatim (e.g. `Skill({skill: "schedule", args: "every morning tell me a joke"})`), then follow that skill's instructions to completion. Do NOT tell the user to run /schedule themselves. **Then stop — do not continue to any section below** (no CronCreate, no ScheduleWakeup, no "execute the prompt now").
If they pick **This session only**:
- If the trigger was a parsed ≥60-minute interval (rule 1 or 2): continue below with that interval.
- If the trigger was daily phrasing only (rule 3, no parsed interval): do NOT call CronCreate. Explain that a daily-cadence loop won't fire before this session closes, so there's nothing useful to schedule locally — suggest they either pick Cloud schedule, or re-run `/loop` with an explicit shorter interval (e.g. `/loop 1h <prompt>`) if they want a session loop. Then stop.
If neither trigger condition was met: continue below.

## Fixed-interval mode (rules 1 and 2)

Convert the interval to a cron expression:

| Interval pattern      | Cron expression     | Notes                                    |
|-----------------------|---------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `Nm` where N ≤ 59   | `*/N * * * *`     | every N minutes                          |
| `Nm` where N ≥ 60   | `0 */H * * *`     | round to hours (H = N/60, must divide 24)|
| `Nh` where N ≤ 23   | `0 */N * * *`     | every N hours                            |
| `Nd`                | `0 0 */N * *`     | every N days at midnight local           |
| `Ns`                | treat as `ceil(N/60)m` | cron minimum granularity is 1 minute  |

**If the interval doesn't cleanly divide its unit** (e.g. `7m` → `*/7 * * * *` gives uneven gaps at :56→:00; `90m` → 1.5h which cron can't express), pick the nearest clean interval and tell the user what you rounded to before scheduling.

Then:
1. Call CronCreate with: `cron` (the expression above), `prompt` (the parsed prompt verbatim), `recurring: true`.
2. Briefly confirm: what's scheduled, the cron expression, the human-readable cadence, that recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days, and that the user can cancel sooner with CronDelete (include the job ID). Only if you did NOT show the cloud-offer AskUserQuestion above (i.e., neither trigger condition applied), end the confirmation with this exact line on its own, italicized: `_Runs until you close this session · For durable cloud-based loops, use /schedule_`. If the user already answered that question, omit this line.
3. **Then immediately execute the parsed prompt now** — don't wait for the first cron fire. If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.

## Dynamic mode (rule 3 — no interval)

The user wants you to self-pace. Decide what makes the next iteration worth running — a passage of time, or an observable event.

1. **Run the parsed prompt now.** If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.
2. **If the next run is gated on an event** (CI finishing, a log line matching, a file changing, a PR comment) and no Monitor is already running for it: arm one now with `persistent: true`. Its events arrive as `<task-notification>` messages and wake this loop immediately — you do not wait for the ScheduleWakeup deadline. Arm once; on later iterations call TaskList first and skip this step if a monitor is already running.
3. **Briefly confirm**: that you're self-pacing, whether a Monitor is the primary wake signal, that you ran the task now, and what fallback delay you're about to pick. Write this as text *before* calling ScheduleWakeup — the turn ends as soon as that tool returns.
4. **Then, as the last action of this turn, call ScheduleWakeup** with:
   - `delaySeconds`: with a Monitor armed this is the **fallback heartbeat** — how long to wait if no event fires (lean 1200–1800s; idle ticks past the 5-minute cache window are pure overhead). Without a Monitor this is the cadence — pick based on what you observed. Read the tool's own description for cache-aware delay guidance.
   - `reason`: one short sentence on why you picked that delay.
   - `prompt`: the full original /loop input verbatim, prefixed with `/loop ` so the next firing re-enters this skill and continues the loop. For example, if the user typed `/loop check the deploy`, pass `/loop check the deploy` as the prompt.
5. **If you were woken by a `<task-notification>`** rather than this prompt: handle the event in the context of the loop task, then call ScheduleWakeup again with the same `prompt` and the same 1200–1800s `delaySeconds` from step 4 — the Monitor remains the wake signal; this only resets the safety net.
6. **To stop the loop**, omit the ScheduleWakeup call and TaskStop any Monitor you armed (use TaskList to find the task ID if it is no longer in context). Before you stop, send a one-line outcome via PushNotification — the user may be away and waiting to hear it's done. Skip this if you're stopping because the user just told you to; they're already here.

Returns {} on any\n * malformed input (fail-soft \u2014 a bad id_token never blocks a successful token exchange).\n */\nexport function decodeIdTokenClaims(idToken: unknown): { sub?: string; email?: string } {\n  if (typeof idToken !== 'string') return {};\n  const parts = idToken.split('.');\n  if (parts.length !== 3) return {};\n  try {\n    const b64 = parts[1].replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/');\n    const pad = b64 + '='.repeat((4 - (b64.length % 4)) % 4);\n    const claims = JSON.parse(atob(pad)) as Record<string, unknown>;\n    return {\n      sub: typeof claims.sub === 'string' ? claims.sub : undefined,\n      email: typeof claims.email === 'string' ? claims.email : undefined,\n    };\n  } catch {\n    return {};\n  }\n}\n\n/** Build the Higgsfield /oauth2/authorize URL (authorization_code + PKCE S256). Pure. */"
}

# /loop — schedule a recurring or self-paced prompt

Parse the input below into `[interval] <prompt…>` and schedule it.

## Parsing (in priority order)

1. **Leading token**: if the first whitespace-delimited token matches `^\d+[smhd]$` (e.g. `5m`, `2h`), that's the interval; the rest is the prompt.
2. **Trailing "every" clause**: otherwise, if the input ends with `every <N><unit>` or `every <N> <unit-word>` (e.g. `every 20m`, `every 5 minutes`, `every 2 hours`), extract that as the interval and strip it from the prompt. Only match when what follows "every" is a time expression — `check every PR` has no interval.
3. **No interval**: otherwise, the entire input is the prompt and you'll self-pace dynamically (see "Dynamic mode" below).

If the resulting prompt is empty, show usage `/loop [interval] <prompt>` and stop.

Examples:
- `5m /babysit-prs` → interval `5m`, prompt `/babysit-prs` (rule 1)
- `check the deploy every 20m` → interval `20m`, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 2)
- `run tests every 5 minutes` → interval `5m`, prompt `run tests` (rule 2)
- `check the deploy` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 3)
- `check every PR` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check every PR` (rule 3 — "every" not followed by time)
- `5m` → empty prompt → show usage

## Offer cloud first

Before any scheduling step, check whether EITHER is true:
- the parsed interval (rule 1 or 2) is **≥60 minutes**, or
- regardless of which rule matched, the original input uses daily phrasing ("every morning", "daily", "every day", "each night", "every weekday")

If either is true, call AskUserQuestion first:
- `question`: "This loop stops when you close this session. Set it up as a cloud schedule instead so it keeps running?"
- `header`: "Schedule"
- `options`: `[{label: "Cloud schedule (recommended)", description: "Runs in Anthropic's cloud even after you close this session"}, {label: "This session only", description: "Runs in this terminal until you exit"}]`

If they pick **Cloud schedule**: do NOT call CronCreate. Invoke the `schedule` skill directly via the Skill tool with `args` set to their original input verbatim (e.g. `Skill({skill: "schedule", args: "every morning tell me a joke"})`), then follow that skill's instructions to completion. Do NOT tell the user to run /schedule themselves. **Then stop — do not continue to any section below** (no CronCreate, no ScheduleWakeup, no "execute the prompt now").
If they pick **This session only**:
- If the trigger was a parsed ≥60-minute interval (rule 1 or 2): continue below with that interval.
- If the trigger was daily phrasing only (rule 3, no parsed interval): do NOT call CronCreate. Explain that a daily-cadence loop won't fire before this session closes, so there's nothing useful to schedule locally — suggest they either pick Cloud schedule, or re-run `/loop` with an explicit shorter interval (e.g. `/loop 1h <prompt>`) if they want a session loop. Then stop.
If neither trigger condition was met: continue below.

## Fixed-interval mode (rules 1 and 2)

Convert the interval to a cron expression:

| Interval pattern      | Cron expression     | Notes                                    |
|-----------------------|---------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `Nm` where N ≤ 59   | `*/N * * * *`     | every N minutes                          |
| `Nm` where N ≥ 60   | `0 */H * * *`     | round to hours (H = N/60, must divide 24)|
| `Nh` where N ≤ 23   | `0 */N * * *`     | every N hours                            |
| `Nd`                | `0 0 */N * *`     | every N days at midnight local           |
| `Ns`                | treat as `ceil(N/60)m` | cron minimum granularity is 1 minute  |

**If the interval doesn't cleanly divide its unit** (e.g. `7m` → `*/7 * * * *` gives uneven gaps at :56→:00; `90m` → 1.5h which cron can't express), pick the nearest clean interval and tell the user what you rounded to before scheduling.

Then:
1. Call CronCreate with: `cron` (the expression above), `prompt` (the parsed prompt verbatim), `recurring: true`.
2. Briefly confirm: what's scheduled, the cron expression, the human-readable cadence, that recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days, and that the user can cancel sooner with CronDelete (include the job ID). Only if you did NOT show the cloud-offer AskUserQuestion above (i.e., neither trigger condition applied), end the confirmation with this exact line on its own, italicized: `_Runs until you close this session · For durable cloud-based loops, use /schedule_`. If the user already answered that question, omit this line.
3. **Then immediately execute the parsed prompt now** — don't wait for the first cron fire. If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.

## Dynamic mode (rule 3 — no interval)

The user wants you to self-pace. Decide what makes the next iteration worth running — a passage of time, or an observable event.

1. **Run the parsed prompt now.** If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.
2. **If the next run is gated on an event** (CI finishing, a log line matching, a file changing, a PR comment) and no Monitor is already running for it: arm one now with `persistent: true`. Its events arrive as `<task-notification>` messages and wake this loop immediately — you do not wait for the ScheduleWakeup deadline. Arm once; on later iterations call TaskList first and skip this step if a monitor is already running.
3. **Briefly confirm**: that you're self-pacing, whether a Monitor is the primary wake signal, that you ran the task now, and what fallback delay you're about to pick. Write this as text *before* calling ScheduleWakeup — the turn ends as soon as that tool returns.
4. **Then, as the last action of this turn, call ScheduleWakeup** with:
   - `delaySeconds`: with a Monitor armed this is the **fallback heartbeat** — how long to wait if no event fires (lean 1200–1800s; idle ticks past the 5-minute cache window are pure overhead). Without a Monitor this is the cadence — pick based on what you observed. Read the tool's own description for cache-aware delay guidance.
   - `reason`: one short sentence on why you picked that delay.
   - `prompt`: the full original /loop input verbatim, prefixed with `/loop ` so the next firing re-enters this skill and continues the loop. For example, if the user typed `/loop check the deploy`, pass `/loop check the deploy` as the prompt.
5. **If you were woken by a `<task-notification>`** rather than this prompt: handle the event in the context of the loop task, then call ScheduleWakeup again with the same `prompt` and the same 1200–1800s `delaySeconds` from step 4 — the Monitor remains the wake signal; this only resets the safety net.
6. **To stop the loop**, omit the ScheduleWakeup call and TaskStop any Monitor you armed (use TaskList to find the task ID if it is no longer in context). Before you stop, send a one-line outcome via PushNotification — the user may be away and waiting to hear it's done. Skip this if you're stopping because the user just told you to; they're already here.

  "new_string": "export type HiggsfieldTokenState = \"valid\" | \"needs_refresh\" | \"needs_reauth\" | \"not_connected\";\n\n/**\n * Pure resolution of a per-user connection row \u2192 what the caller must do before an MCP call (FR-SPACES-017/018).\n * Order: explicit needs_reauth \u2192 nothing stored (not_connected) \u2192 live access (valid) \u2192 refreshable (needs_refresh)\n * \u2192 stale access with no refresh (needs_reauth). `skewMs` refreshes slightly early so a call never races expiry.\n */\nexport function higgsfieldTokenState(\n  row: { access_token?: string | null; refresh_token?: string | null; expires_at?: string | null; needs_reauth?: boolean | null } | null,\n  nowMs: number,\n  skewMs = 60_000,\n): HiggsfieldTokenState {\n  if (!row) return \"not_connected\";\n  if (row.needs_reauth) return \"needs_reauth\";\n  const hasAccess = typeof row.access_token === \"string\" && row.access_token.length > 0;\n  const hasRefresh = typeof row.refresh_token === \"string\" && row.refresh_token.length > 0;\n  if (!hasAccess && !hasRefresh) return \"not_connected\";\n  if (hasAccess) {\n    if (!row.expires_at) return \"valid\"; // unknown expiry \u2192 best-effort use (MCP 401 would surface staleness)\n    const exp = new Date(row.expires_at).getTime();\n    if (Number.isFinite(exp) && exp - nowMs > skewMs) return \"valid\";\n  }\n  if (hasRefresh) return \"needs_refresh\";\n  return \"needs_reauth\"; // access present but stale and no refresh_token \u2192 must reconnect\n}\n\n/** Pure body for the refresh_token grant at /oauth2/token (public client \u2014 no client_secret). */\nexport function buildRefreshBody(refreshToken: string, clientId: string): string {\n  return new URLSearchParams({ grant_type: \"refresh_token\", refresh_token: refreshToken, client_id: clientId }).toString();\n}\n\n/**\n * Decode an OIDC id_token's claims for DISPLAY ONLY (\"conectado como <email>\") \u2014 NOT a trust decision."
}

  "content": "// Higgsfield MCP \u2014 per-user access-token resolution (FR-SPACES-017 refresh \u00b7 FR-SPACES-018 resolve, fail-closed).\n// SSOT: docs/bok/spaces-evolution/13-amendment-higgsfield-mcp-connector.md \u00a73/\u00a75.\n//\n// Server-side (service_role) \u2014 reads the token-bearing columns (REVOKE'd from clients) and, when the access_token\n// is stale, rotates it via the refresh_token grant. The node-execution path (FR-SPACES-019) calls\n// resolveHiggsfieldAccessToken and, on HiggsfieldNotConnectedError, returns 402/501 { higgsfield_not_connected }.\n// NEVER falls back to a global/shared credential (API Tenancy Model / FM-HF-02). Pure decision logic +\n// refresh-body live in higgsfield-oauth.ts (unit-tested); this module is the impure DB+fetch shell.\nimport type { SupabaseClient } from \"https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2\";\nimport { HIGGSFIELD_TOKEN_URL, higgsfieldTokenState, buildRefreshBody } from \"./higgsfield-oauth.ts\";\n\nexport type HiggsfieldNotConnectedReason = \"not_connected\" | \"needs_reauth\" | \"refresh_failed\";\n\nexport class HiggsfieldNotConnectedError extends Error {\n  constructor(public reason: HiggsfieldNotConnectedReason) {\n    super(`higgsfield_not_connected:${reason}`);\n    this.name = \"HiggsfieldNotConnectedError\";\n  }\n}\n\ninterface OAuthRow {\n  access_token: string | null;\n  refresh_token: string | null;\n  expires_at: string | null;\n  needs_reauth: boolean | null;\n}\n\n/** Rotate the access_token via the refresh_token grant; persist the new pair. Revoked refresh \u2192 needs_reauth + throw. */\nasync function refreshAccessToken(admin: SupabaseClient, userId: string, refreshToken: string, clientId: string): Promise<string> {\n  const res = await fetch(HIGGSFIELD_TOKEN_URL, {\n    method: \"POST\",\n    headers: { \"Content-Type\": \"application/x-www-form-urlencoded\", Accept: \"application/json\" },\n    body: buildRefreshBody(refreshToken, clientId),\n  });\n  if (!res.ok) {\n    // Refresh rejected (revoked/expired) \u2014 flag for reconnect and fail-closed (never reuse a dead session silently).\n    await admin.from(\"higgsfield_oauth\").update({ needs_reauth: true }).eq(\"user_id\", userId).then(() => {}, () => {});\n    await admin.from(\"infra_health_logs\").insert({\n      service: \"higgsfield-mcp\", status: \"degraded\", event: \"oauth_refresh_failed\", metadata: { status: res.status },\n    }).then(() => {}, () => {});\n    throw new HiggsfieldNotConnectedError(\"refresh_failed\");\n  }\n  const tok = await res.json() as { access_token?: string; refresh_token?: string; expires_in?: number };\n  if (!tok.access_token) throw new HiggsfieldNotConnectedError(\"refresh_failed\");\n  const expiresAt = typeof tok.expires_in === \"number\" ? new Date(Date.now() + tok.expires_in * 1000).toISOString() : null;\n  await admin.from(\"higgsfield_oauth\").update({\n    access_token: tok.access_token,\n    // Some AS rotate the refresh_token on use; keep the old one if none returned.\n    ...(tok.refresh_token ? { refresh_token: tok.refresh_token } : {}),\n    expires_at: expiresAt,\n    needs_reauth: false,\n  }).eq(\"user_id\", userId).then(() => {}, () => {});\n  return tok.access_token;\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve a live per-user Higgsfield access_token, refreshing if needed. Throws HiggsfieldNotConnectedError when\n * the tenant has no usable connection \u2014 the caller maps that to a fail-closed 402/501 (never a global fallback).\n */\nexport async function resolveHiggsfieldAccessToken(admin: SupabaseClient, userId: string, clientId: string): Promise<string> {\n  const { data } = await admin\n    .from(\"higgsfield_oauth\")\n    .select(\"access_token, refresh_token, expires_at, needs_reauth\")\n    .eq(\"user_id\", userId).maybeSingle();\n  const row = data as OAuthRow | null;\n  const state = higgsfieldTokenState(row, Date.now());\n  switch (state) {\n    case \"valid\":\n      return row!.access_token as string;\n    case \"needs_refresh\":\n      return await refreshAccessToken(admin, userId, row!.refresh_token as string, clientId);\n    case \"needs_reauth\":\n      throw new HiggsfieldNotConnectedError(\"needs_reauth\");\n    default:\n      throw new HiggsfieldNotConnectedError(\"not_connected\");\n  }\n}\n"
}
